changes: The flat map is now a real 3D sandstone garden with three terrace heights, visible stairs on disclosed legal passages, original articulated Pip and Thornback models, keys, gates, traps and an exit portal.
Follow, Detail and Overview cameras, a public-data map, optional original audio, captions, reduced motion, high contrast and clean feed are integrated.

Graphics loss reveals a live map, offers a retry and returns to the current public position after restoration. Real results remain visible in map mode; reconnecting is now explicit during terminal states.
Cumulative steps and discovered area reflect the public snapshot. Character feet, route marks, lights and camera targets follow the same stair heights.

Pip now has a coral scarf and bedroll, clearer eyes and directional gaze; Thornback has a broader bronze face and brighter eyes. Fresh actual portrait, desktop, detail and encounter captures are recorded.

Keys have a thicker silhouette and readable sway; the exit has a mint opening and diamond crown. Quieter trim, grouped planting and shoreline contacts are implemented. The mobile critic still wants stronger objective contrast and clearer local intent.

Map and Path notes expand on demand, while the goal and immediate intent stay visible. Natural captions replace internal object IDs, and the camera label says Detail. Browser checks verify disclosure drawing, Escape/focus and terminal reconnect; a fresh blind critic preferred the compact mobile layout.

A fifth-pass encounter-staging candidate now gives Pip threat-directed head, gaze and lantern poses, and Thornback anticipatory mask/mandible poses, using only disclosed nearby threats. Fresh render and independent critique are still pending.
nextGaps: Capture the new public-threat encounter poses and shared framing in real running desktop and mobile output; a fresh independent critic must compare label-masked round-04 versus this candidate and then judge Captain Toad directly.
Make the immediate objective, obstacle and route more legible in the world; increase key contrast and clarify why another key is needed when one has already been collected.
Develop a more distinctive landmark or encounter and the explorer’s target-directed expression at normal viewing size.
Review fresh real motion for gait, turns, stair contact and reactions, and independently listen to the audio mix.
Capture current full-quality output and measure representative hardware performance; retain the existing test budgets and fixed bar.
Continue the builder and fresh-critic loop from the largest observed gap, using the pinned reference images; no fixed round count and no benchmark reduction.

reviews.title: Environment comparison · first pass
reviews.summary: The scene still reads as a repetitive flat maze board. Improve architectural hierarchy, focal landmarks, garden scale and material richness. The fixed bar has not been lowered.

reviews.title: Environment comparison · second pass
reviews.summary: The candidate remains a shallow corridor network. Substantial architecture, quieter water, stronger material separation and grouped foliage are the highest-value changes.

reviews.title: Character comparison · first pass
reviews.summary: The 3D explorer has a distinct identity, but the amber/ivory body merges into sandstone at gameplay scale. Broader colour masses, simpler facial detail and clearer pose are needed; warden and motion evidence pending.

reviews.title: Integrated terraced scene · third pass
reviews.summary: Real 3D world and developed explorer/beetle characters are supported by the inspected captures. Captain Toad still wins on landmark composition, connected materials, expression and use of screen space. The comparison was explicitly unblinded because the reference is recognizable; the later fourth-pass changes have not been judged.

reviews.title: Portrait composition · blind A/B
reviews.verdict: Latest version wins A/B; reference still wins
reviews.summary: The critic selected anonymous B, the fourth pass, before seeing version identity: more scene height, larger explorer, clearer objective and less persistent interface. Remaining gaps are distinctive local staging, expressive action, key contrast and an explicit relationship between the current goal and collected inventory.

reviews.title: Current world and characters · blind A/B
reviews.verdict: Latest version wins narrowly; reference still wins
reviews.summary: Anonymous A, the fourth pass, has a clearer key, explorer face, quieter planting and more natural captions. The guardian encounter is nearly tied with the prior version. The fixed reference still leads in expressive encounter staging, distinctive landmarks and character/material separation.

reviews.title: Fifth-pass CI capture — initial artifact inspection (not independent)
reviews.reviewer: Lead inspection of actual CI screenshots; fresh-context critic not available
reviews.verdict: No new fixed-bar verdict; encounter staging remains open
reviews.summary: The current-source 1920×1080 and 1280×720 views show an original terraced garden, Pip, a disclosed beetle guardian and a stage route, but the actors are widely separated. These frames do not show proximity-triggered attention or an actionable encounter moment. Prior independent fourth-pass critics still prefer the official Nintendo reference. A separate blind A/B critic is required.
